[odoo/TECHNICAL_NOTE.md](odoo/TECHNICAL_NOTE.md#L1), and the Workflows in [odoo/_workflows/WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md](odoo/_workflows/WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md#L1).\n\n**Architecture & Patterns**\n- **Module split**: `sports_federation_base` (master data), `sports_federation_tournament` (tournaments, matches, participants), `sports_federation_format / sports_federation_scheduling` (service/wizards), plus domain modules (`people`, `rules`, `officiating`, `rosters`, `result_control`, `public_site`, `reporting`, `finance_bridge`, `venues`, `discipline`, `standings`, ...).\n- **Model naming**: Domain models use the `federation.` prefix (e.g. `federation.player`, `federation.match`).\n- **Common patterns**: `ir.sequence` for identifiers, `state` selection fields for workflows, wizards for batch operations (under `wizards/`), `controllers/` for portal/website endpoints, and `security/` for groups/record rules/ACLs.\n\n**Key Files & Where To Look**\n- **High-level context**: [odoo/CONTEXT.md](odoo/CONTEXT.md#L1)\n- **Technical architecture**: [odoo/TECHNICAL_NOTE.md](odoo/TECHNICAL_NOTE.md#L1)\n-- **Workflows (authoritative behavioural spec)**: `README.md` under `odoo/<module>/README.md` with implementation notes and expectations.\n-- **Install logs / historical notes**: `_logs/` contains installation and setup notes per module.\n\n**Development Guidelines (how to implement changes)**\n- **Add/modify a model**: create/modify `models/*.py`, export package in `models/__init__.py`, add access rules in `security/ir.model.access.csv`, add any initial `data/*.xml` and register them in `__manifest__.py` `data` or `demo` lists, add views in `views/*.xml`, update `menu_items.xml` as needed, and add tests under `tests/`.\n- **Add a wizard or service**: put transient models under `wizards/` and views under `views/` (manifest `data`), keep service logic in modules like `sports_federation_format / sports_federation_scheduling` (no persistent models if not required).\n- **Add a controller / portal flow**: use `controllers/` and add templates under `views/` or `templates/`; respect portal record rules (see `sports_federation_portal`).\n- **Security**: always add or update `security/ir.model.access.csv` and any `security/*.xml` groups/rules for new models or new endpoints.\n- **Manifest  {"content": "# ADR-0002: Reporting SQL Views\n\nLast updated: 2026-04-18\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-20\nReview cadence: Every release\nStatus: Accepted\n\n## Context\n\nFederation reporting combines finance, standings, compliance, notification, planning, and workflow data across multiple addons. Rebuilding those joins in controllers or repeated ORM loops would duplicate logic and create unpredictable performance.\n\n## Decision\n\nOperational and planning projections remain read-only analytical models backed by PostgreSQL views when their data is naturally cross-module or aggregation-heavy.\n\n- SQL-backed report models use `_auto = False`.\n- View definitions are recreated deterministically from `init()` or the repository's approved view helper.\n- Controllers and exports consume report models instead of embedding substantial SQL or cross-module aggregation logic.\n- Report models are read-only and must not masquerade as writable business records.\n- Heavy reports retain query budgets, representative fixtures, and performance watchpoints.\n- SQL view changes are upgrade-sensitive and require migration review evidence.\n- A normal stored Odoo model is preferred when the data has its own lifecycle or must be edited.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Cross-module reporting logic remains centralized.\n- Export and operator surfaces share the same projection semantics.\n- View dependencies and upgrade order require explicit review.\n- Maintainers must preserve query plans, migration safety, and read-only behavior.\n", "content_length": 1514, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "adr/0002-reporting-sql-views.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "ef36c1653fd664b1b66d727fab316472e1dd05aad0b7e71a28d0f01cd5a889ad", "size_bytes": 1514}
 {"content": "# ADR-0003: Public Route Ownership\n\nLast updated: 2026-04-18\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-20\nReview cadence: Every release\nStatus: Accepted\n\n## Context\n\nPublic tournament pages, feeds, calendars, registration entry points, and compatibility aliases can collide when several addons define overlapping controllers. Numeric legacy routes also create ambiguity about the canonical public contract.\n\n## Decision\n\n- `/competitions` and `/competitions/<edition-slug>` are the canonical public page routes.\n- Tournament-named page routes are compatibility redirects only.\n\nPublic route ownership is tournament-first and module-explicit:\n\n- `sports_federation_public_site` owns canonical public competition pages and match-day publication views; legacy tournament feeds and calendars remain compatibility contracts.\n- Slug-first routes are canonical for new consumers.\n- Numeric and competition-named routes may remain only as documented compatibility aliases with an owner and review date.\n- Public reads enforce applicable publication controls such as `website_published`, `show_public_results`, and `show_public_standings`.\n- Public write entry points use a model-owned request boundary and must not broaden portal or backend privileges.\n- Route inventory, OpenAPI contracts, compatibility notes, and smoke coverage are part of the ownership boundary.\n- Duplicate or shadow public controllers are removed rather than kept as silent fallbacks.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Controller precedence and deprecation become reviewable.\n- New public surfaces must update route and contract documentation in the same change.\n- Compatibility routes carry an explicit maintenance cost and sunset decision.\n- Publication defaults remain deny-by-default.\n", "content_length": 1753, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "adr/0003-public-route-ownership.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "8f2952d166f7cf414b532edcbbe59159565833ea88c150bdc2b4a5248d639a7d", "size_bytes": 1753}

 {"content": "# Sports Federation Format\n\nThe format addon manages versioned competition structures, their stages, and\nFormat Studio stage graphs.\n\n## Stage graph models\n\nFormat Studio uses `federation.structure.stage.progression` for edges between\nstages in one `federation.competition.structure`. This is deliberately\nseparate from the competition engine's `federation.stage.progression` model,\nwhich belongs to tournament-level progression workflows and uses a different\nrelation contract.\n\nBefore generating a structure, the graph is validated for cycles. Root stages\ncan then be prepared; dependent stages wait for incoming progression results.\nApproved fixture results can populate dependent stages, and frozen standings\nare stored as immutable snapshots.\n\nStage-graph access rules are loaded from `security/ir.model.access.csv`. The\nstructure form extension identifies the stage tab by its `stage_ids` field so\nthe view remains safe when translated page labels change.\n## Supported format generation\n\nThe format studio now estimates fixture and round counts before generation. It supports single and double leagues, seeded knockout and placement brackets, match series, pool-to-knockout configuration, championship/relegation splits, Swiss rounds, ladder formats, and power-of-two double elimination. Swiss round counts are configurable on the structure, while double elimination uses the dynamic pairing service to account for its winner, loser, and reset-final routes. These estimates are planning guidance; format-specific generation workflows remain responsible for validating the final fixture graph.\n", "content_length": 1599, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_format/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "a77ea3a8e64ed4bd839025fe8e3e21961d32e160ec3c607bd480eaa5b7eb539d", "size_bytes": 1599}

 {"content": "Sports Federation Import Tools\n==============================\n\nWizard-driven CSV import for clubs, seasons, teams, players, and tournament\nparticipants. The module is intended for federation onboarding and annual\nrollover work where administrators need rehearsable imports instead of raw ORM\nloads.\n\nPurpose\n-------\n\nThe import wizards provide a safer operator workflow than direct list imports:\n\n- dry-run rehearsal before any records are created\n- approval checkpoints before live imports execute\n- visible column mapping guidance in the wizard form\n- code-first reference lookup where the target models expose stable codes\n- categorized row-level failures instead of opaque batch errors\n- duplicate-safe behavior that reports and skips existing records\n- reusable template records that define the import contract per wizard\n- governance-job verification summaries with before/after target counts\n- managed partner contracts with token-authenticated subscriptions\n- staged inbound deliveries that reuse the same governed preview and approval\n  pipeline\n\nThe menu entry is available at ``Federation > Import Tools``.\nThe transient import models now live under the standard ``wizards/`` package to\nmatch the rest of the repository.\n\nDependencies\n------------\n\n- ``sports_federation_base``: Clubs, seasons, teams.\n- ``sports_federation_people``: Players.\n- ``sports_federation_tournament``: Tournament participants.\n\nShared Wizard Behaviour\n-----------------------\n\nAll import wizards inherit ``federation.import.wizard.mixin``.\n\nShared capabilities:\n\n- UTF-8 and UTF-8 BOM CSV decoding.\n- Comma or semicolon delimiter support.\n- Reusable ``federation.import.template`` selection.\n- Checksum-bound ``federation.import.job`` approval workflow for live imports.\n- Shared fields: ``dry_run``, ``mapping_guide``, ``result_message``,\n  ``line_count``, ``success_count``, and ``error_count``.\n- Shared ``_execute_row_create(...)`` handling so live imports reuse one\n  row-create failure path instead of ad hoc wizard-level try/except blocks.\n- Standardized error categories such as ``missing_reference``,\n  ``duplicate_entry``, ``format_error``, and ``missing_required_field``.\n- Explicit compatibility handling for legacy CSV aliases tracked in\n  ``INTEGRATION_CONTRACTS.md``.\n\nManaged Partner Integrations\n----------------------------\n\nThe module also provides a managed integration layer for machine-driven import\nand export contracts.\n\nCore models:\n\n- ``federation.integration.contract`` defines the contract code, version,\n  direction, transport, route hint, availability requirements, and optional\n  linked import template.\n- ``federation.integration.partner`` stores partner identity, token rotation,\n  and delivery history.\n- ``federation.integration.partner.contract`` records which contracts a partner\n  is allowed to use.\n- ``federation.integration.delivery`` stages inbound partner payloads and links\n  them to the downstream governance job.\n\nCurrent model layout:\n\n- ``models/integration_contract.py`` keeps contract manifest and availability\n  rules.\n- ``models/integration_partner.py`` keeps partner identity, subscription\n  lookup, and the stable authentication entry point.\n- ``models/integration_partner_token_mixin.py`` keeps token generation,\n  hashing, verification, migration, and hashed persistence hooks.\n- ``models/integration_partner_rotation_mixin.py`` keeps manager-driven token\n  rotation and audit logging.\n- ``models/integration_partner_contract.py`` keeps subscription state and usage\n  tracking.\n- ``models/integration_delivery.py`` keeps the ORM fields and composes focused\n  helper mixins.\n- ``models/integration_delivery_stage_mixin.py`` keeps inbound staging,\n  idempotency, duplicate reuse, and attachment creation.\n- ``models/integration_delivery_workflow_mixin.py`` keeps wizard handoff and\n  delivery state transitions.\n- ``models/integration_delivery_retention_mixin.py`` keeps retention cleanup.\n\nCurrent wizard layout:\n\n- ``wizards/import_wizard_mixin.py`` remains the stable shared surface used by\n  all import wizards.\n- ``wizards/import_wizard_csv_mixin.py`` keeps CSV parsing, column validation,\n  row helpers, and shared error taxonomy.\n- ``wizards/import_wizard_governance_mixin.py`` keeps approval checks,\n  governance-job persistence, and result finalization.\n\nCurrent controller layout:\n\n- ``controllers/integration_api.py`` keeps the stable public route surface and\n  route-level orchestration.\n- ``controllers/integration_api_auth_mixin.py`` keeps header parsing, partner\n  authentication, caller identity, and rate-limit subject helpers.\n- ``controllers/integration_api_response_mixin.py`` keeps JSON response\n  shaping and typed error payload helpers.\n\nPhased Maintainability Plan\n---------------------------\n\n- Initial completed: the former multi-model gateway hotspot was split into\n  per-model files without changing model names, fields, or table ownership.\n  Test impact: existing import-tools tests should stay green. Migration risk:\n  none, because this is a file-layout change only.\n- Rules completed: delivery staging, idempotency, workflow handoff, and\n  retention cleanup now live in dedicated helper mixins while\n  ``federation.integration.delivery`` keeps the ORM contract stable. Test\n  impact: inbound delivery staging, idempotency, and retention coverage stays\n  green. Migration risk: replay semantics and attachment linkage.\n- Integration completed: token generation, hashing, verification, migration, and\n  rotation or audit helpers now live in dedicated partner mixins while\n  ``federation.integration.partner`` keeps the stable ORM entry points for\n  authentication and subscription lookup. Test impact: token rotation and\n  legacy-token migration coverage stay green. Migration risk: stored hash\n  compatibility and audit logging.\n- API completed: ``wizards/import_wizard_mixin.py`` now composes dedicated\n  CSV and governance or result helper mixins while preserving the shared wizard\n  API. Test impact: shared mixin coverage plus wizard-specific dry-run and\n  live-import flows stay green. Migration risk: approval checksum binding and\n  result-summary compatibility.\n- Operations completed: ``controllers/integration_api.py`` now composes dedicated\n  auth and response helper mixins while preserving the public route surface and\n  existing headers and status codes. Test impact: integration API credential,\n  rate-limit, finance export, and inbound delivery coverage stays green.\n  Migration risk: request patching in tests and route-level error semantics.\n\nManaged Integration Behaviour\n-----------------------------\n\n- Authentication: partners use ``X-Federation-Partner-Code`` plus either\n  ``X-Federation-Partner-Token`` or ``Authorization: Bearer <token>``.\n- Contract manifest: ``/integration/v1/contracts`` exposes the subscribed\n  contract manifest, including database-specific availability and deprecation\n  metadata.\n- Inbound deliveries: ``/integration/v1/inbound/<contract_code>/deliveries``\n  stores staged deliveries with checksum-based duplicate reuse and can bind an\n  ``X-Federation-Idempotency-Key`` for safe retries.\n- Operator workflow: operators open the staged delivery directly in the\n  matching import wizard, review the preview, request approval, and then run\n  the live import.\n- Auditability: delivery records mirror preview, approval, completion, and\n  failure states so the inbound handoff remains auditable.\n\nManaged Integration Contract Docs\n---------------------------------\n\n- Narrative policy and deprecation guidance live in\n  ``INTEGRATION_CONTRACTS.md``.\n- Machine-readable route and payload definitions live in\n  ``openapi/integration_v1.yaml``.\n- Partner onboarding golden examples live in\n  ``openapi/examples/INTEGRATION_GOLDEN_EXAMPLES.md``.\n\nCorrelation ID Standard\n-----------------------\n\n- Managed integration routes accept optional\n  ``X-Federation-Correlation-Id`` headers.\n- JSON responses include ``correlation_id`` and mirror it in the\n  ``X-Federation-Correlation-Id`` response header.\n- CSV exports include ``X-Federation-Correlation-Id`` for cross-service\n  traceability.\n- Typed JSON error payloads include ``error``, ``error_code``, and\n  ``correlation_id``.\n\nCredential Handling\n-------------------\n\n- Partner secrets are stored hashed at rest; the raw token is never shown\n  again after issuance.\n- Federation managers issue or rotate a token from the partner form, then copy\n  it from the one-time modal.\n- Each manager-driven token rotation writes a shared audit event that appears\n  in ``Reporting > Token Rotation Audit``.\n- URL query parameters are rejected for partner authentication to avoid\n  leaking secrets into logs, browser history, or proxy traces.\n- Legacy plaintext tokens are migrated into hashed storage on module load and\n  flagged for mandatory rotation.\n\nInbound Delivery Guardrails\n---------------------------\n\n- Partner uploads must use a ``.csv`` filename and a ``text/csv`` content type\n  when declared.\n- Inbound payloads larger than 5 MiB are rejected before staging.\n- Duplicate inbound payloads are deduplicated by checksum before a new\n  delivery record or attachment is created.\n- Explicit inbound idempotency keys replay the original delivery across\n  retries and reject conflicting payload reuse.\n- Successful inbound API responses expose ``delivery_outcome`` plus\n  ``X-Federation-Delivery-Outcome`` so clients can distinguish fresh staging\n  from checksum reuse and idempotent replay.\n- Terminal inbound deliveries are purged automatically once they exceed the\n  retention windows documented in ``DATA_RETENTION_POLICY.md``; the staged\n  payload attachment is deleted with the delivery record.\n\nSupported Wizards\n-----------------\n\n``federation.import.clubs.wizard``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nRequired columns:\n\n- ``name``\n\nRecommended columns:\n\n- ``code``, ``email``, ``phone``, ``city``\n\nDuplicate matching:\n\n- ``code`` first, then exact club ``name``\n\n``federation.import.seasons.wizard``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nRequired columns:\n\n- ``name``, ``code``, ``date_start``, ``date_end``\n\nOptional columns:\n\n- ``state``, ``notes``, ``target_club_count``, ``target_team_count``,\n  ``target_tournament_count``, ``target_participant_count``\n\nValidation notes:\n\n- Dates must use ``YYYY-MM-DD``.\n- State must be one of ``draft``, ``open``, ``closed``, or ``cancelled``.\n- Planning target columns must be whole numbers greater than or equal to zero.\n\n``federation.import.teams.wizard``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nRequired columns:\n\n- ``team_name`` or ``name``\n- ``club_code`` or ``club_name``\n\nRecommended columns:\n\n- ``code``, ``category``, ``gender``, ``email``, ``phone``\n\nDuplicate matching:\n\n- ``code`` first, then ``(club_id, name)``\n\n``federation.import.players.wizard``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nRequired columns:\n\n- ``first_name`` and ``last_name``\n- Legacy imports may use ``name`` when it contains both parts of the full name.\n\nRecommended columns:\n\n- ``birth_date``, ``club_code`` or ``club_name``, ``gender``, ``email``,\n  ``phone``, ``state``\n\nValidation notes:\n\n- ``birth_date`` must use ``YYYY-MM-DD``.\n- Duplicate detection follows the player uniqueness key:\n  ``(first_name, last_name, ``team_code`` or ``team_name``\n\nOptional columns:\n\n- ``seed``\n\nValidation notes:\n\n- Team eligibility and duplicate participation reuse the same tournament-side\n  checks as manual participant creation.\n\nOperational Behaviour\n---------------------\n\n- Dry-run imports validate every row and never create records.\n- Live imports require an approved governance job tied to the current file\n  checksum and template.\n- Real imports create valid rows and keep processing after row-level failures.\n- Existing records are not overwritten; duplicates are reported and skipped.\n- Result summaries include both totals and categorized error counts so\n  administrators can fix the source CSV predictably.\n- Governance jobs store preview totals plus before or after record counts for\n  post-import verification.\n- Staged partner deliveries can enter the same preview and approval workflow\n  without bypassing governance controls.\n- Delivery failures and partial-import outcomes  {"content": "# Match-Day Operations\n\nThis addon executes the current immutable schedule publication. It never edits\napproved publication evidence.\n\n## Operator workflow\n\n- **Match-Day Control** shows readiness and the exact live publication.\n- **Open Match Day** validates the publication digest and creates an immutable\n  execution session.\n- Court status and incidents are changed through command-backed wizards.\n- Operational schedule changes support move, delay, postpone and cancel.\n- Every deviation requires a reason and records the session, publication, actor,\n  old slot and new slot.\n- The immutable `published_slot_id` is preserved. Live reality is represented by\n  `operational_slot_id` and `operational_status`.\n- Normal close requires all matches finished or cancelled and all incidents\n  resolved. Forced close requires a reason.\n\n## Validation\n\n```bash\npython ci/check_schedule_handoff_contract.py\npython ci/check_publication_integrity_contract.py\nbash ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_schedule_approval\nbash ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_matchday\n```\n\n## Restarting unpublished planning\n\nMatch-day managers can use **Restart from Scratch** before any schedule review or\npublication evidence exists. The action requires a reason and explicit destructive\nconfirmation, removes mutable schedules and the old match day, then creates and\nopens a clean replacement with the same edition, date, venue, and slot defaults.\nDirect deletion of a draft match day also removes its draft or change-requested\nworking schedules first. Published, reviewed, open, and closed match days remain\nprotected and must use the normal revision or operational correction workflows.\n\n## Deleting closed test data\n\nFederation managers and match-day managers can use **Delete Match Day** on a\nclosed match day. The confirmation wizard shows the number of schedules,\npublications, execution sessions, deviations, and matches affected. Confirming\nthe deletion permanently removes the match-day planning and execution evidence;\nlinked match records remain in the competition but are detached from the deleted\npublication and calendar slots. The action requires a reason and displays a\nfinal confirmation popup before deletion.\n\n\n\n## Transactional operational commands\n\nMatch-day opening, court status changes, incident resolution, operational match\ndeviations, session closure, and match-day closure use the shared workflow\ntransition service. Every public command runs inside a database savepoint and\nreturns a structured result containing the affected record IDs, actor, and\nresulting state. Forced closure requires a reason. Published schedule evidence\nremains immutable and deviations alter operational fields only.\n\nTransition failures roll back sessions, court statuses, operational match\nchanges, incidents, and audit rows as one unit.\n", "content_length": 2837, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_matchday/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "235fd541df3b077c4cce593311c179e194a7b1cec95660d1455230d2d014a024", "size_bytes": 2837}

 {"content": "\"\"\"Tour T-04: Roster Management — Activation, Match Sheet Workflow, Close\n\nWalks the full roster lifecycle for a team:\n  1. Draft roster — activation fails without players\n  2. Add players, activate roster\n  3. Unique-active-roster constraint: second activation attempt raises\n  4. Create a match and a match sheet linked to the active roster\n  5. Add lines (roster players) to the sheet\n  6. Submit → approve → lock the match sheet (match must be done)\n  7. Close the roster at season end\n\nKey invariants verified:\n- Draft roster with no lines cannot be activated\n- Once active, roster can be closed\n- Match sheet follows: draft → submitted → approved → locked\n- Lock requires match in 'done' state\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom odoo.exceptions import ValidationError\nfrom odoo.tests.common import TransactionCase\n\n\nclass TestTourRosterLifecycle(TransactionCase):\n    \"\"\"T-04: Roster lifecycle and match sheet workflow tour.\"\"\"\n\n    @classmethod\n    def setUpClass(cls):\n        super().setUpClass()\n\n        cls.club = cls.env[\"federation.club\"].create(\n            {\"name\": \"Roster Tour Club\", \"code\": \"RCLB\"}\n        )\n        cls.team = cls.env[\"federation.team\"].create(\n            {\"name\": \"Roster Tour Team\", \"club_id\": cls.club.id, \"code\": \"RTT26\"}\n        )\n        cls.season = cls.env[\"federation.season\"].create(\n            {\n                \"name\": \"Roster Tour Season\",\n                \"code\": \"RST26\",\n                \"date_start\": \"2026-01-01\",\n                \"date_end\": \"2026-12-31\",\n            }\n        )\n        rule_set = cls.env[\"federation.rule.set\"].create(\n            {\n                \"name\": \"Roster Tour Rules\",\n                \"code\": \"RSTR\",\n                \"points_win\": 3,\n                \"points_draw\": 1,\n                \"points_loss\": 0,\n            }\n        )\n        tournament = cls.env[\"federation.tournament\"].create(\n            {\n                \"name\": \"Roster Tour Cup\",\n                \"date_start\": \"2026-03-01\",\n                \"rule_set_id\": rule_set.id,\n            }\n        )\n        cls.tournament = tournament\n        cls.rule_set = rule_set\n\n        # Create players\n        cls.players = cls.env[\"federation.player\"]\n        for i in range(1, 5):\n            p = cls.env[\"federation.player\"].create(\n                {\n                    \"first_name\": f\"Roster{i}\",\n                    \"last_name\": \"Player\",\n                    \"gender\": \"male\",\n                }\n            )\n            cls.players |= p\n\n    def test_roster_lifecycle_and_match_sheet_workflow(self):\n        \"\"\"Roster draft → activate → match sheet full lifecycle → close.\"\"\"\n\n        # STEP 1: Empty roster cannot be activated\n        roster = self.env[\"federation.team.roster\"].create(\n            {\n                \"name\": \"Tour Roster\",\n                \"team_id\": self.team.id,\n                \"season_id\": self.season.id,\n                \"min_players_required\": 0,\n            }\n        )\n        self.assertEqual(roster.status, \"draft\")\n        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):\n            roster.action_activate()\n\n        # STEP 2: Add players and activate\n        lines = self.env[\"federation.team.roster.line\"]\n        for player in self.players:\n            line = self.env[\"federation.team.roster.line\"].create(\n                {\n                    \"roster_id\": roster.id,\n                    \"player_id\": player.id,\n                    \"status\": \"active\",\n                }\n            )\n            lines |= line\n        roster.action_activate()\n        self.assertEqual(roster.status, \"active\")\n\n        # STEP 3: Create a match in 'done' state (needed to lock sheet later)\n        match = self.env[\"federation.match\"].create(\n            {\n                \"tournament_id\": self.tournament.id,\n                \"home_team_id\": self.team.id,\n                \"home_score\": 3,\n                \"away_score\": 1,\n                \"state\": \"done\",\n            }\n        )\n\n        # STEP 4: Create match sheet using side='other' to avoid team constraint\n        sheet = self.env[\"federation.match.sheet\"].create(\n            {\n                \"match_id\": match.id,\n                \"team_id\": self.team.id,\n                \"side\": \"other\",\n                \"roster_id\": roster.id,\n            }\n        )\n        self.assertEqual(sheet.state, \"draft\")\n\n        # STEP 5: Add lines — each references a roster line for eligibility\n        for player, line in zip(self.players, lines):\n            self.env[\"federation.match.sheet.line\"].create(\n                {\n                    \"match_sheet_id\": sheet.id,\n                    \"player_id\": player.id,\n                    \"roster_line_id\": line.id,\n                    \"is_starter\": True,\n                }\n            )\n\n        # STEP 6: Submit\n        sheet.action_submit()\n        self.assertEqual(sheet.state, \"submitted\")\n\n        # STEP 7: Approve\n        sheet.action_approve()\n        self.assertEqual(sheet.state, \"approved\")\n\n        # STEP 8: Lock (match is already 'done')\n        sheet.action_lock()\n        self.assertEqual(sheet.state, \"locked\")\n        self.assertTrue(sheet.locked_on)\n        self.assertTrue(sheet.locked_by_id)\n\n        #  {"content": "# Sports Federation Scheduling\n\nThe scheduling addon owns working schedules, fixture assignments, schedule\nchanges, and the weighted fairness auto-schedule preview.\n\nThe auto-schedule wizard previews deterministic assignments after applying hard\nconstraints and weighted fairness penalties. Applying a proposal records the\nautomatic assignments and schedule changes while checking the schedule revision\nfor concurrent edits.\n\nAll access-control rows, including the auto-schedule wizard permissions, are\nloaded through `security/ir.model.access.csv`.\n\n\n## Operator handoff to independent review\n\nA planner completes fixture-to-slot assignments in **Schedule Planner** and uses\n**Submit for Review**. Blocking validation errors prevent submission. When only\nwarnings remain, a confirmation dialog requires an explicit justification. The\nbutton delegates to `federation.schedule.commands`; when Schedule Approval is\ninstalled, the approval extension creates the immutable pending review in the\nsame transaction and opens it directly.\n\nSubmitted schedules are immutable. If a reviewer requests changes, the schedule\nreturns to `changes_requested`, where the planner can edit and submit a new\nrevision. Planners can use the **Reviews** smart button to inspect the current\nhandoff and retained history.\n\n\n## Reversible planning\n\nDraft and change-requested schedules refresh the current calendar fixture pool. Late fixtures appear as unassigned work; stale assignments are flagged and never silently deleted. Pending submissions can be withdrawn, while published corrections use governed replacement revisions.\n\n\n## Multi-division match days\n\nA working schedule covers the complete physical match day, not only the division structure that originally opened the planner. If another division is allocated to the same match day during a governed revision, **Refresh Calendar Fixtures** exposes those fixtures as unassigned work and auto-scheduling includes them in its proposal. Submission remains blocked until every non-bye fixture from every match-day allocation is assigned.\n\nPublication validates the current match-day fixture pool again. If allocations change after review, publication stops and requires a refreshed, complete schedule and a new review instead of silently publishing an incomplete game day.\n\n## Club-aware automatic scheduling\n\nAutomatic scheduling treats simultaneous matches involving different teams of\nthe same club as the first fairness priority. It detects any overlapping slot\nwindows, not only slots with identical boundaries. After deterministic greedy\nconstruction, a bounded pairwise-swap improvement pass repairs avoidable club\nclashes while preserving all hard constraints and pinned manual or operational\nassignments. Remaining club clashes therefore indicate constrained capacity or\npinned assignments rather than an avoidable greedy choice.\n\n", "content_length": 2871, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_scheduling/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "01a61a812eeb85aef16c2a4468df9e02429b7f4c71152a09e06f997ff9a92a93", "size_bytes": 2871}

 {"content": "# Sports Federation Tournament\n\nTournament lifecycle management — from creation through scheduling to completion.\nProvides the structural backbone for all competitive activity: tournaments, stages,\ngroups, participants, and matches.\n\n## Purpose\n\nModels the full **tournament hierarchy**: a tournament is divided into stages\n(e.g. group phase, quarter-finals), stages contain groups, and groups contain\nmatches between participants. This module is the central hub that most\ncompetition-related modules extend.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n| Module | Reason |\n|--------|--------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Clubs, teams, seasons |\n| `sports_federation_rules` | Rule sets, competitions |\n\n## Models\n\n### `federation.competition`\n\nA named competition series (e.g. \"National League Division 1\") that may span\nmultiple seasons and link to a rule set.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` / `code` | Char | Competition identity |\n| `season_id` | Many2one | Governing season |\n| `rule_set_id` | Many2one | Applicable rule set |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / active / closed |\n| `tournament_ids` | One2many | Tournaments under this competition |\n\n### `federation.season` extension\n\nThe module extends seasons with a tournament relation and a dedicated tournament\ncount stat used by the season form shortcut into related tournaments.\n\n### `federation.tournament`\n\nA single tournament event within a competition or season.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` / `code` | Char | Tournament identity |\n| `season_id` | Many2one | Season context |\n| `competition_id` | Many2one | Parent competition |\n| `rule_set_id` | Many2one | Rules (inherited from competition or set directly) |\n| `tournament_type` | Selection | league / cup / friendly / playoff |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / open / in_progress / closed / cancelled |\n| `date_start` / `date_end` | Date | Event window |\n| `max_participants` | Integer | Participant cap |\n| `stage_ids` | One2many | Tournament stages |\n| `participant_ids` | One2many | Enrolled participants |\n| `match_ids` | One2many | All matches across stages |\n\n- **State machine**: draft → open → in_progress → closed / cancelled.\n- **Stat buttons** for stages, participants, and matches.\n\n### `federation.tournament.stage`\n\nA phase or round within a tournament (e.g. \"Group Phase\", \"Semi-finals\").\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Stage label |\n| `tournament_id` | Many2one | Parent tournament |\n| `stage_type` | Selection | group / knockout / playoff / other |\n| `sequence` | Integer | Natural ordering |\n| `date_start` / `date_end` | Date | Stage window |\n| `group_ids` | One2many | Groups within this stage |\n| `match_ids` | One2many | Matches in this stage |\n\n### `federation.tournament.group`\n\nA subdivision within a stage (e.g. \"Group A\", \"Pool 1\").\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Group label |\n| `stage_id` | Many2one | Parent stage |\n| `tournament_id` | Many2one | Computed from stage |\n| `sequence` | Integer | Natural ordering |\n| `max_participants` | Integer | Group capacity |\n| `participant_ids` | One2many | Teams in this group |\n| `match_ids` | One2many | Group matches |\n\n### `federation.tournament.participant`\n\nLinks a team to a tournament, optionally assigned to a specific stage and group.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char (computed) | Team name in tournament context |\n| `tournament_id` | Many2one | Tournament |\n| `team_id` | Many2one | The team |\n| `club_id` | Many2one | Computed from team |\n| `stage_id` / `group_id` | Many2one | Assignment |\n| `seed` | Integer | Seeding rank |\n| `registration_date` | Date | When enrolled |\n| `state` | Selection | registered / confirmed / withdrawn / eliminated |\n\n### `federation.match`\n\nAn individual game between two teams.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char (computed) | \"Home vs Away\" |\n| `tournament_id` | Many2one | Tournament |\n| `stage_id` / `group_id` | Many2one | Location in hierarchy |\n| `round_id` | Many2one | Single-day round assignment |\n| `home_team_id` / `away_team_id` | Many2one | Competing teams |\n| `date_scheduled` | Datetime | Stored kickoff datetime for downstream integrations |\n| `scheduled_date` | Date (computed) | Inherited from the assigned round |\n| `scheduled_time` | Float | Editable match kickoff time-of-day |\n| `home_score` / `away_score` | Integer | Final score |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / scheduled / in_progress / done / cancelled |\n\n- **State machine**: draft → scheduled → in_progress → done / cancelled.\n\n## Key Behaviours\n\n1. **Hierarchical structure** — Tournament → Stage → Group → Match.\n2. **Participant tracking** — Teams enrol in a tournament and are placed into stages/groups.\n3. **Score entry** — Match results are recorded with home/away scores.\n4. **State management** — Both tournaments and matches follow state machines that\n   prevent illogical transitions.\n5. **Round-owned scheduling** — Rounds are single-day containers. A match assigned to a round inherits that round's calendar date and only stores its own kickoff time.\n6. **Stage windows** — Stages remain the broader multi-day grouping above rounds.\n7. **Tournament open/start guards** — Only active draft tournaments linked to a season can open, and only open tournaments with at least one stage can start.\n8. **Archive safety** — Open or in-progress tournaments must be closed or cancelled before archiving.\n9. **Venue extensions** — Venue fields are supplied by `sports_federation_venues`; this module keeps the core match lifecycle and hierarchy only.\n\n## Migration note (v19.0.1.1.0)\n\n- Added migration scripts under `migrations/19.0.1.1.0/` to harden `federation.match` indexing for high-traffic filters.\n- Added backfill for `scheduled_date` and `round_number` on historical match rows where those persisted values were missing.\n- Added composite indexes for `(tournament_id, state)`, `(stage_id, state)`, `(group_id, state)`, `(scheduled_date, state)`, and `(date_scheduled, state)`.\n\n## Knockout result resolution (v19.0.1.2.0)\n\nKnockout matches must have an unambiguous advancing team before they can be\ncompleted. A tied numeric score requires a non-regulation resolution, such as\novertime, tiebreak, forfeit, walkover, or an administrative decision, plus an\nexplicit advancing team selected from the two match participants.\n\nWinner and loser bracket progression uses this explicit decision, preventing a\ncompleted knockout match from leaving downstream participants unresolved.\n", "content_length": 6639, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_tournament/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "3bf73f9207c54b0d3b527f74a84d44b7e21e216f6a3f91489177bce88e6b76a3", "size_bytes": 6677}

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Verify that release browser dependencies are locked into the CI image."""
+
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import sys
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+EXPECTED = "websocket-client==1.8.0"
+
+
+def find_violations(root: Path = ROOT) -> list[str]:
+    requirements = root / "requirements.txt"
+    runtime_requirements = root / "requirements-odoo-ci.txt"
+    dockerfile = root / "ci/Dockerfile.odoo-ci"
+    compose = root / "ci/docker-compose.ci.yaml"
+    violations = []
+    if not requirements.is_file() or EXPECTED not in requirements.read_text():
+        violations.append(f"requirements.txt must lock {EXPECTED}")
+    if (
+        not runtime_requirements.is_file()
+        or EXPECTED not in runtime_requirements.read_text()
+    ):
+        violations.append(f"requirements-odoo-ci.txt must lock {EXPECTED}")
+    if not dockerfile.is_file():
+        violations.append("the Odoo CI Dockerfile is missing")
+    else:
+        source = dockerfile.read_text()
+        if "sports-federation-odoo-ci-requirements.txt" not in source:
+            violations.append(
+                "the Odoo CI image does not install its runtime requirements"
+            )
+        if "requirements.txt /tmp" in source:
+            violations.append(
+                "the Odoo CI image must not install host lint requirements"
+            )
+        if "import websocket" not in source:
+            violations.append("the Odoo CI image does not verify websocket-client")
+    if not compose.is_file():
+        violations.append("the CI Compose file is missing")
+    else:
+        source = compose.read_text()
+        if not re.search(r"dockerfile:\s+ci/Dockerfile\.odoo-ci", source):
+            violations.append("ci-odoo does not build the locked Odoo CI image")
+    return violations
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    violations = find_violations()
+    if violations:
+        print("Browser runtime contract failed:", file=sys.stderr)
+        for violation in violations:
+            print(f"- {violation}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+    print("Browser runtime contract passed.")
+    return 0
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     raise SystemExit(main())

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Classify a failed release lane from its focused log evidence."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+from pathlib import Path
+
+RULES = (
+    ("unsupported_configuration", ("websocket-client module is not installed", "browser test dependency")),
+    ("documentation_drift", ("documentation freshness", "broken markdown link", "delivery language")),
+    ("migration_defect", ("migration", "upgrade failed", "invariant mismatch", "rollback")),
+    ("performance_regression", ("performance regression", "query budget exceeded")),
+    ("fixture_defect", ("duplicate key value violates unique constraint", "fixture setup")),
+    ("test_defect", ("test collection", "test discovery", "no tests were found")),
+    ("infrastructure_defect", ("docker is required", "connection refused", "timed out", "no space left")),
+    ("product_defect", ("fail:", "error:", "validationerror", "assertionerror")),
+)
+
+
+def classify(log_text: str, lane: str = "") -> str:
+    text = log_text.lower()
+    if lane == "preflight" and "release workspace contains tracked changes" in text:
+        return "unsupported_configuration"
+    for classification, patterns in RULES:
+        if any(pattern in text for pattern in patterns):
+            return classification
+    return "unclassified"
+
+
+def main() -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--log", required=True, type=Path)
+    parser.add_argument("--lane", default="")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    text = args.log.read_text(errors="replace") if args.log.is_file() else ""
+    print(classify(text, args.lane))
+    return 0
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     raise SystemExit(main())
